lessons.title: Sound recognition: vowel sounds
lessons.objective: Distinguish single vowel sounds (monophthongs), double vowel sounds (diphthongs) and triple vowel sounds (triphthongs) and pronounce them well.
lessons.course:
Some vowel sounds are single: the sound in “sit”, “bed”, “cup”, “food”. Some glide from one sound to another (diphthongs): “day”, “eye”, “boy”, “go”, “cow”. A few glide through three sounds (triphthongs): “fire”, “hour”, “player”.
Good pronunciation helps people understand us, for example at the clinic: “pain”, “cough”, “fever”.
lessons.model: The adult says “bed” (one sound) and “day” (the voice glides). The children feel the difference with a hand under the chin.
lessons.guided: Listen to pairs of words and say whether the vowel sound is single or gliding: bed/day, cup/cow, sit/sight.
lessons.exercise: Is the vowel sound in “boy” single or gliding?
lessons.remediation: Work with three diphthongs only: day, eye, boy.
lessons.transfer: Find three health words with a gliding vowel sound (pain, eye, nose).

practice.prompt: Listen and repeat the words. Which one has a gliding sound?
Which word has a triphthong (three sounds)?
practice.explanation: fire: the voice glides through three sounds.

practice.prompt: Sort: single or gliding?
practice.answer: sit: single; go: gliding; cup: single.

lessons.title: Reading a short story silently: at the health centre
lessons.objective: Read a short story silently and answer literal and inference questions.
lessons.course: Some answers are written in the text (literal questions). Others must be guessed from clues (inference questions): “Why was Enow sad?” We look for clues and explain with “because”.

support.title: Read silently
support.text: Enow woke up with a high fever and a headache. His mother touched his forehead and took him to the health centre. The nurse tested his blood and said, “It is malaria.” She gave him tablets and told him to sleep under a mosquito net every night. After three days, Enow went back to school, but he kept the net over his bed.

lessons.model: The adult reads silently, then says: “The text says he had a fever — that is literal. He kept the net — I guess he did not want to be sick again — that is inference.”
lessons.guided: Read silently. Answer two literal questions and one inference question.
lessons.exercise: What did the nurse say Enow had?
lessons.remediation: Underline the answers in the text before saying them.
lessons.transfer: Read a health leaflet with an adult and say one thing you learnt.

practice.prompt: What two symptoms did Enow have?
practice.answer: A high fever and a headache.
accept: a high fever and a headache
A high fever and a headache
practice.explanation: It is written in the first sentence.

practice.prompt: Why did Enow keep the net over his bed?
choices: so that he would not get malaria again
practice.answer: so that he would not get malaria again
practice.explanation: Inference: the net protects from mosquitoes.

practice.prompt: How many days later did Enow go back to school?
practice.explanation: The text says: After three days.

lessons.title: Dictation: sentences and a short paragraph
lessons.objective: Write dictated sentences and a short paragraph with correct spelling and punctuation.
lessons.course:
During a dictation, we listen to the whole sentence first, then write group of words by group of words. We check capital letters, full stops and difficult words.
Before the dictation, we study the difficult words: healthy, vegetables, every, enough, water.

support.title: Words to study
support.text: healthy  vegetables  every  enough  water  fruit

lessons.model: The adult reads a sentence once, then in groups of words, then once more to check.
lessons.guided: Study the words, then listen to the dictation and write. Check with the text.
lessons.exercise: Spell the word we study: v-e-g-…
lessons.remediation: Do the dictation one sentence at a time, checking after each one.
lessons.transfer: Ask an adult to dictate two sentences to you each day.

practice.prompt: Listen to the dictation and write it.
practice.listen: To stay healthy, we eat fruit and vegetables every day. We drink enough clean water.
practice.answer: To stay healthy, we eat fruit and vegetables every day. We drink enough clean water.
practice.explanation: Check capitals, commas and full stops.

practice.prompt: Which word is spelt correctly?
Put the steps of a dictation in order.

lessons.title: Pronouns: subject, object and possessive
lessons.objective: Use subject, object and possessive pronouns correctly.
lessons.course:
Subject pronouns do the action: I, you, he, she, it, we, they. She helps the nurse.
Object pronouns receive the action: me, you, him, her, it, us, them. The nurse helps her.
Possessive pronouns show who owns: mine, yours, his, hers, ours, theirs. This net is mine.
lessons.model: The adult points: “He gives the tablets to her. The tablets are hers now.”
lessons.guided: Replace nouns with pronouns in five sentences about a visit to the clinic.
lessons.exercise: Replace the words: The doctor examined Enow. → The doctor examined ___.
lessons.remediation: Practise subject pronouns, then object pronouns, before possessives.
lessons.transfer: Tell a short story about your family using he, she, him, her.

practice.prompt: Complete with the right pronoun.
practice.text: Mama gave the medicine to [[us]]. [[We]] took it after the meal.
practice.explanation: us is an object; we is a subject.

practice.prompt: Which word is a possessive pronoun?
Match the subject pronoun with its object pronoun.
practice.explanation: Each subject pronoun has an object form.

lessons.title: Proper fractions
lessons.objective: Read, write and represent proper fractions of a whole.
lessons.course:
A fraction is a part of a whole divided into equal parts. In ¾, the denominator (4) is the number of equal parts; the numerator (3) is the number of parts taken.
In a proper fraction, the numerator is smaller than the denominator: ½, ⅓, ¾, ⅖.
lessons.model: The adult cuts a pawpaw into 4 equal parts and takes 3: “three quarters, ¾”.
lessons.guided: Fold paper into 2, 4 and 8 equal parts. Shade parts and write the fraction.
lessons.exercise: A cake is cut into 8 equal pieces. Bih eats 3. What fraction did she eat?
lessons.remediation: Use halves and quarters with real fruit first.
lessons.transfer: Find fractions at home: half a loaf, a quarter of an orange.

practice.prompt: In ⅗, what is the denominator?
practice.explanation: The denominator is the bottom number.

practice.prompt: Which one is a proper fraction?
Shade 3/4 of a rectangle cut into 4 equal parts.

lessons.title: Adding and subtracting fractions with the same denominator
lessons.objective: Add and subtract fractions that have the same denominator.
lessons.course:
When the denominators are the same, we add or subtract the numerators and keep the denominator: 2/7 + 3/7 = 5/7; 5/8 − 2/8 = 3/8.
If the result equals the denominator, we have one whole: 3/5 + 2/5 = 5/5 = 1.
lessons.model: A nurse gives 1/4 of a bottle of syrup in the morning and 2/4 in the evening: 3/4 of the bottle.
lessons.guided: Use paper strips divided into eighths to add and subtract fractions.
lessons.remediation: Shade the parts on a strip before calculating.
lessons.transfer: Share a fruit and say what fraction was eaten and what is left.

practice.prompt: Complete.
Manka drinks 2/5 of her water. What fraction is left?

lessons.title: Finite and infinite sets; elements and symbols
lessons.objective: Distinguish finite and infinite sets and use the symbols ∈, ∉ and Ø.
lessons.course:
A finite set has a number of elements we can count: {days of the week} has 7 elements. An infinite set never ends: {1, 2, 3, 4, …}.
∈ means “is an element of”: Monday ∈ {days of the week}. ∉ means “is not an element of”. Ø or { } is the empty set: {children in our class older than 50 years} = Ø.
lessons.guided: Sort sets into finite or infinite. Write three sentences with ∈ and ∉.
lessons.exercise: Is the set of even numbers finite or infinite?
lessons.remediation: Count the elements of small sets to see that they end.
lessons.transfer: Give an example of an empty set in your home.

practice.prompt: Which set is finite?
practice.explanation: There are 12 months: we can count them.

practice.prompt: Complete with ∈ or ∉.
How many elements does the empty set have?
practice.explanation: The empty set has no element.

lessons.title: Ranking data in ascending and descending order
lessons.objective: Rank data in ascending and descending order and read a table.
lessons.course:
Ascending order goes from the smallest to the biggest; descending order from the biggest to the smallest.
A table of data: children vaccinated at the health centre — Monday 34, Tuesday 52, Wednesday 27, Thursday 45. In descending order: 52, 45, 34, 27.
lessons.model: The adult ranks the days from the busiest to the quietest at the health centre.
lessons.guided: Rank the heights or ages of family members in both orders.
lessons.remediation: Compare two numbers at a time.
lessons.transfer: Rank the prices of five things in a shop.

practice.prompt: Put in descending order.
Which day had the fewest vaccinations?
How many more children on Tuesday than on Monday?
